preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.strip()) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit())
preconditions.description: Every integer in the input (T, Q, and each X) is a positive integer within the bounds 1 ≤ X, Q ≤ 10^5 and 1 ≤ T ≤ 5.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == 1 + sum(int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), 2)) + sum(1 for i in range(2, len(stdin.splitlines()), 2) if stdin.splitlines()[i].strip().isdigit())
preconditions.description: The input format is valid: T lines for test cases, each followed by Q lines of X values, with no malformed lines.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and line.split()[0].isdigit() and line.split()[1].isdigit() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip())
postconditions.description: For each query, the output is a single line with two space-separated integers E and O, representing the counts of elements in S with even and odd numbers of 1s in their binary representation, respectively.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(E) + int(O) <= 10**5 for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() for E, O in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: The sum of E and O for each query equals the size of S after processing the query, and both are non-negative integers.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda S: sum(1 for x in S if bin(x).count('1') % 2 == 0), sum(1 for x in S if bin(x).count('1') % 2 == 1)) == (int(E), int(O)) for S, line in zip([set()], [set()]) for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() for E, O in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: For each query, the output (E, O) correctly counts the elements in S with even and odd numbers of 1s in their binary representation, where S is the set after processing all queries up to and including the current one.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda S, X: S.union({X}).union({y ^ X for y in S if y != X})) == S_next for S, S_next in zip([set()], [set()]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() for X in [int(line)] for S_next in [set()])
postconditions.description: The set S evolves correctly: for each query X, S is updated by adding X and all y ^ X for y in S before the query (excluding X itself).
